title: contour
body:
## contour

Extracts isosurfaces (3-D input) or isolines (2-D input) where a point-centred scalar field equals each of the given values, and outputs them as polydata; several values give several surfaces in one output. Use it for level sets such as a temperature front or a Q-criterion vortex surface. By Schemaxis default the output carries normals and the contour value as an array, but no gradients. Use pvContour for the full native settings.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The scalar must be point data; for cell arrays run cellToPoint first.
- Values outside the field's range produce an empty output without an error.

Native constructor: `Contour`. Identity: `curated binding`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input dataset to be used by the contour filter. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet); hyper-tree grids (adaptive AMR-like trees) (vtkHyperTreeGrid). The input needs at least one point-centred array with 1 component (for vtkDataSet input). The input needs at least one cell-centred array with 1 component (for vtkHyperTreeGrid input). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet","vtkHyperTreeGrid"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | Select the association and scalar array whose level surfaces will be extracted. Point scalars are the usual input; convert cell arrays when required. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"minItems":2,"maxItems":2}` | `required` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE","REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `values` | One or more scalar levels to extract. Choose values within the actual input range and in that field’s units. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":1}` | `required` | `[1]` |
| `normals` | If this property is set to 1, a scalar array containing a normal value at each point in the isosurface or isoline will be created by the contour filter; otherwise an array of normals will not be computed. This operation is fairly expensive both in terms of computation time and memory required, so if the output dataset produced by the contour filter will be processed by filters that modify the dataset's topology or geometry, it may be wise to set the value of this property to 0. Select whether to compute normals. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `true` | `true` |
| `gradients` | If this property is set to 1, a scalar array containing a gradient value at each point in the isosurface or isoline will be created by this filter; otherwise an array of gradients will not be computed. This operation is fairly expensive both in terms of computation time and memory required, so if the output dataset produced by the contour filter will be processed by filters that modify the dataset's topology or geometry, it may be wise to set the value of this property to 0. Not that if ComputeNormals is set to 1, then gradients will have to be calculated, but they will only be stored in the output dataset if ComputeGradients is also set to 1. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` | `false` |
| `scalars` | If this property is set to 1, an array of scalars (containing the contour value) will be added to the output dataset. If set to 0, the output will not contain this array. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `true` | `true` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "contour",
  "inputs": {
    "input": "UPSTREAM_input"
  },
  "options": {
    "field": [
      "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE",
      "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
    ],
    "values": [
      1
    ]
  }
}
```
